text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said the government would soon enact laws to recover looted money.
- The Deputy Prime Minister of Australia Tim Fischer said the Australian investment in Pakistan would increase five-fold to one billion Australian dollars in 1997.
- Indian and Pakistani foreign ministers are expected to meet in New Delhi next week after a Non-Aligned Movement ministerial conference there on April 7-8.
- Nawaz Sharif has directed state-run Pakistan International Airlines to induct six Jumbo 747s and two Boeing 777 aircrafts in its fleet by December 1998 at a cost of $1.0 billion.
- The wheat flour shortage in the North West Frontier Province sparked violence in Peshawar and some other parts of the province.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has raised the forward cover fee by a quarter percent on dollar deposits ostensibly in anticipation of a marginal rupee devaluation.
- The government has formed a panel of economists to prepare ninth five-year plan to formulate a vision of economy by the year 2010 in terms off targets and benchmarks.
- The State (central) Bank has turned down the request of ginners for relaxation in the payment of mark-up on unsold cotton, ginners said.
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub left for New Delhi on his first major diplomatic assignment which includes a non-agenda meeting with his Indian counterpart I.K. Gujral.
- U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan has urged India and Pakistan to press ahead with bilateral talks, saying he was excited by the prospects of peace in the volatile region.
